q-130569.name: Question 1
q-130569.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=2$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{x+7}+{4}^{x} \\ f(2) & =\sqrt{2+7}+{4}^{2} \\  & =\sqrt{9}+16 \\  & =3+16 \\  & =19\end{aligned}
$$

q-130574.name: Question 2
q-130574.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=2$ and $y=1$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =(x-3y)(x+y)^{2} \\ f(2,1) & =(2-3(1))(2+1)^{2} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (3)^{2} \\  & =-1\cdot 9 \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

f(x,y)=(x−3y)(x+y)2f(2,1)=(2−3(1))(2+1)2=(−1)⋅(3)2=−1⋅9=−9

q-130578.name: Question 3
q-130578.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=1$ and $y=1$ into the function definition and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =(3y-x)^{3}+(2x-y)^{2} \\ f(1,1) & =(3(1)-1)^{3}+(2(1)-1)^{2} \\  & ={2}^{3}+{1}^{2} \\  & =8+1 \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$
